html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • The marker carries the message (Coder_Msg_Ready)
  • A bottle is marked (the marker's count moves)
  • The camera inspects a bottle (Cam1:I.Inspection_ID counts up)
  • A result is acknowledged (Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack)
  • A defective bottle is pushed into Reject_Bin
  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (55 s)

Hard · par 55 s

The job

Level 8’s line with one lot and a serial on every bottle. The PLC gives the laser marker each bottle’s serial before the bottle reaches it (Serial_No with Lot_No 151, then Load_Msg and wait for Msg_Ready): the marker marks L0151-001, L0151-002 … one serial per bottle, never twice. The camera’s code-verify job reads the mark back and sends the string it read in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27 (L at 12, the lot at 13-16, the serial at 18-20; NOREAD when it read nothing). Compare it with the serial you sent for that bottle (it rides in a FIFO from the marker to the camera): a mismatch is a reject, and Mismatch_Count counts every one (it is on the console). The marker misprints a digit now and then, misses a mark, and its window fumes up after so many marks (faint marks the camera cannot read: Lamp_Lens on Window_Dirty and the operator cleans it three seconds later). Three mismatches in a row are not three bad bottles: stop the line (Lamp_Fault) until START. +100 per right bin, −100 for a bottle shipped with a misprinted, missing or repeated code, −50 for a good bottle rejected.

The program

The marker needs each bottle’s serial before the bottle reaches it: the program moves the next serial into Serial_No with the lot, pulses Load_Msg and waits for Msg_Ready before it releases the bottle. The serial rides a FIFO from the marker to the camera. When the camera’s result comes in, the program turns the characters it read (bytes 12 to 27 of Inspection_Results) back into numbers, each digit’s character code minus 48, and compares the serial with the one unloaded from the FIFO. A mismatch, a NOREAD or a defect bit marks the bottle for the reject pusher and counts in Mismatch_Count; three in a row stop the line on Lamp_Fault until START, because three bad codes in a row are a marker problem, not three bad bottles.

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

The rungs

Watch for

A character in a byte array is its character code, not its digit: the camera’s 1 arrives as 49. Subtract 48 before you compare it with a number.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in; a code fault drops it

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off, E_Stop is on and Code_Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off, E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on and Code_Fault (Three mismatches in a row: the line stops until START) is off, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. XIO(Code_Fault) Examine If Open asks: true when Code_Fault is off.
  5. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt and the run lamp follow Run
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled, results buffered

pred.q: E_Stop is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is off and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is off. It stops at XIC(E_Stop).

rungs.words: When E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: LASER: armed while the line runs
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Laser_On (Laser marker: arm the laser (its interlock); no mark while 0) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Laser_On) Output Energize does: turns Laser_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: THE LOT: one lot today, 151. Every bottle carries it, with its own serial
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung puts 151 into Coder_Lot (Laser marker: the lot number for the message).
rungs.ltr: 1. MOV(151,Coder_Lot) Move does: puts 151 into Coder_Lot. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: RELEASE: a bottle every 0.9 s while the hopper exit is clear
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is off, the rung runs the timer Rel_T (Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) toward 900 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Rel_T.DN is off.
  4. TON(Rel_T,900,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Rel_T toward 900 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Rel_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: One bottle out, and the next serial with it into the hopper-to-marker FIFO. The branches run top to bottom, so the FFL loads the serial the ADD has just made
rungs.words: When Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is on, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false), makes Next_Ser (The serial of the last bottle released) = Next_Ser + 1 and loads Next_Ser into the queue Ser_Q[0] (The serials of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rel_T.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. ADD(Next_Ser,1,Next_Ser) Add does: makes Next_Ser = Next_Ser + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. FFL(Next_Ser,Ser_Q[0],Ser_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Next_Ser into the queue Ser_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.why: Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: THE MESSAGE: once the bottle under the head has gone, the marker is told the serial of the next one (the oldest in the FIFO). Not while a bottle is under it: that bottle's mark is still to come
rungs.words: When PE_Coder (The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head) is off, Ser_Q_Ctl.POS (the position of Ser_Q_Ctl: FIFO control for Ser_Q) is greater than 0 and Coder_Serial (Laser marker: the serial for the message (loaded with Load_Msg)) is not Ser_Q[0] (The serials of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first), the rung puts Ser_Q[0] into Coder_Serial.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Coder) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Coder is off.
  2. GRT(Ser_Q_Ctl.POS,0) Greater Than asks: true when Ser_Q_Ctl.POS is greater than 0.
  3. NEQ(Coder_Serial,Ser_Q[0]) Not Equal asks: true when Coder_Serial is not Ser_Q[0].
  4. MOV(Ser_Q[0],Coder_Serial) Move does: puts Ser_Q[0] into Coder_Serial. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: Load the message whenever it does not carry Lot_No and Serial_No: a rising edge of Load_Msg, 0.3 s, then Msg_Ready
rungs.words: When Coder_Msg_Ready (Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No) is off, Coder_Ready (Laser marker ready: armed and not loading) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Coder_Load (Laser marker: load Lot_No into the message (rising edge, 0.5 s)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Coder_Msg_Ready) Examine If Open asks: true when Coder_Msg_Ready is off.
  2. XIC(Coder_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Coder_Ready is on.
  3. ONS(Load_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Load_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. OTE(Coder_Load) Output Energize does: turns Coder_Load on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: AT THE MARKER: a bottle arrives; the oldest serial is its serial. It goes on to the marker-to-camera FIFO: that is what the camera must read
rungs.words: When PE_Coder (The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Ser_Q[0] (The serials of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first) into Mark_Ser (The serial of the bottle at the marker) and loads Mark_Ser into the queue Cam_Q[0] (The serials marked, between the marker and the camera, oldest first).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Coder) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Coder is on.
  2. ONS(Mark_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Mark_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFU(Ser_Q[0],Mark_Ser,Ser_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Ser_Q[0] into Mark_Ser. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. FFL(Mark_Ser,Cam_Q[0],Cam_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Mark_Ser into the queue Cam_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: MARK: the message loaded and carrying this bottle's serial

pred.q: PE_Coder is on, Coder_Msg_Ready is on, Coder_Serial is 31 and Mark_Ser is 43. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Coder_Mark is off. It stops at EQU(Coder_Serial,Mark_Ser).

rungs.words: When PE_Coder (The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head) is on, Coder_Msg_Ready (Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No) is on and Coder_Serial (Laser marker: the serial for the message (loaded with Load_Msg)) equals Mark_Ser (The serial of the bottle at the marker), the rung turns Coder_Mark (Laser marker: mark the message on the bottle under the head (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Coder) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Coder is on.
  2. XIC(Coder_Msg_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Coder_Msg_Ready is on.
  3. EQU(Coder_Serial,Mark_Ser) Equal asks: true when Coder_Serial equals Mark_Ser. Both values are compared every scan.
  4. OTE(Coder_Mark) Output Energize does: turns Coder_Mark on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: A BOTTLE AT THE CAMERA: it wants an inspection, and the serial it should carry comes out of the FIFO
rungs.words: When PE_Trigger (Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) on and unloads the oldest entry of Cam_Q[0] (The serials marked, between the marker and the camera, oldest first) into Cam_Ser (The serial the camera should read on the bottle it is inspecting).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Trigger is on.
  2. ONS(Trig_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Trig_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Trig_Req) Output Latch does: latches Trig_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. FFU(Cam_Q[0],Cam_Ser,Cam_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Cam_Q[0] into Cam_Ser. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.why: Trig_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: TRIGGER when the camera is ready

pred.q: Trig_Req is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready).

rungs.words: When Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  3. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: Acknowledged: drop the trigger
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger and unlatches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Trig_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Trig_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: THE READ-BACK: the string the camera read is in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27, one character a byte: L0151-007 is L at 12, the lot at 13-16, the dash at 17, the serial at 18-20. A digit is its character code minus 48 ('0' is 48), so the lot and the serial come back as numbers. NOREAD (nothing read) gives nonsense numbers, which is right: they will not match
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung computes Read_Lot (The lot read back: characters 2-5) = (Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[13]-48)*1000+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[14]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[15]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[16]-48, computes Read_Ser (The serial read back: characters 7-9 of the string in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27) = (Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[18]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[19]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[20]-48 and puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Res_Code (The result of the bottle just inspected: the camera's bits, plus 128 for a mismatch).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. CPT(Read_Lot,(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[13]-48)*1000+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[14]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[15]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[16]-48) Compute does: computes Read_Lot = (Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[13]-48)*1000+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[14]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[15]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[16]-48.
    Path 2
    1. CPT(Read_Ser,(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[18]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[19]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[20]-48) Compute does: computes Read_Ser = (Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[18]-48)*100+(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[19]-48)*10+Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[20]-48.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Res_Code) Move does: puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Res_Code. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: MISMATCH: the serial or the lot read back is not what was sent
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on, Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off and either (Read_Ser (The serial read back: characters 7-9 of the string in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27) is not Cam_Ser (The serial the camera should read on the bottle it is inspecting)) or (Read_Lot (The lot read back: characters 2-5) is not 151), the rung turns Mismatch (The read-back is not what was sent) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. NEQ(Read_Ser,Cam_Ser) Not Equal asks: true when Read_Ser is not Cam_Ser.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(Read_Lot,151) Not Equal asks: true when Read_Lot is not 151.
  4. OTE(Mismatch) Output Energize does: turns Mismatch on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: A mismatch is a reject (bit 7 of the result), it is counted, and the run of mismatches grows

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on, Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off and Mismatch is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: OR runs, Mismatch_Count is written and Mis_Run is written.

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on, Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off and Mismatch (The read-back is not what was sent) is on, the rung makes Res_Code (The result of the bottle just inspected: the camera's bits, plus 128 for a mismatch) = Res_Code OR 128, bit by bit, makes Mismatch_Count (Shown on the toolbar and the console: marks that did not read back as sent) = Mismatch_Count + 1 and makes Mis_Run (Mismatches in a row) = Mis_Run + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. XIC(Mismatch) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mismatch is on.
  4. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OR(Res_Code,128,Res_Code) Bitwise Or does: makes Res_Code = Res_Code OR 128, bit by bit.
    Path 2
    1. ADD(Mismatch_Count,1,Mismatch_Count) Add does: makes Mismatch_Count = Mismatch_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. ADD(Mis_Run,1,Mis_Run) Add does: makes Mis_Run = Mis_Run + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: A good read ends the run
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on, Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off and Mismatch (The read-back is not what was sent) is off, the rung clears Mis_Run (Mismatches in a row) to 0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. XIO(Mismatch) Examine If Open asks: true when Mismatch is off.
  4. CLR(Mis_Run) Clear does: clears Mis_Run to 0.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: The result into the FIFO to the pusher, and the acknowledge (last: the rungs above read the result while Results_Valid is on and the ack is still off)
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung loads Res_Code (The result of the bottle just inspected: the camera's bits, plus 128 for a mismatch) into the queue Res_Q[0] (The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) and latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Res_Code,Res_Q[0],Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Res_Code into the queue Res_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: Results_Valid down: ack down
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: THREE IN A ROW: three bottles do not all come wrong by chance. The marker (its window, its head) or the camera is the problem: stop the line

pred.q: Mis_Run is 2. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Code_Fault is left as it was. It stops at GEQ(Mis_Run,3).

rungs.words: When Mis_Run (Mismatches in a row) is at least 3, the rung latches Code_Fault (Three mismatches in a row: the line stops until START) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. GEQ(Mis_Run,3) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Mis_Run is at least 3.
  2. OTL(Code_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Code_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Code_Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: START clears the fault: the operator has looked
rungs.words: When Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on and Run (Seal-in run bit) is off, the rung unlatches Code_Fault (Three mismatches in a row: the line stops until START) and clears Mis_Run (Mismatches in a row) to 0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
  2. XIO(Run) Examine If Open asks: true when Run is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Code_Fault) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Code_Fault. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. CLR(Mis_Run) Clear does: clears Mis_Run to 0.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Code_Fault when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 22
rungs.comment: AT THE REJECT PUSHER: the oldest result is this bottle's
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] (The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) into Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Res_Q[0],Cur,Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: Any bit, the mismatch included: arm the pusher
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on, this is the first scan of it and Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher) is not 0, the rung latches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS2) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS2). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. NEQ(Cur,0) Not Equal asks: true when Cur is not 0.
  4. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 24
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye

pred.q: PE_Reject is on and Fire is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Reject is on.

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 25
rungs.comment: Count it
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, it makes Reject_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected) = Reject_Count + 1; if Fire is off, it makes Pass_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through) = Pass_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
    2. ADD(Reject_Count,1,Reject_Count) Add does: makes Reject_Count = Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fire) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire is off.
    2. ADD(Pass_Count,1,Pass_Count) Add does: makes Pass_Count = Pass_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 26
rungs.comment: The bottle has gone: disarm

pred.q: PE_Reject is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fire is left as it was. It stops at XIO(PE_Reject).

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 27
rungs.comment: WINDOW: the lamp calls the operator, who cleans the window three seconds after it lights
rungs.words: When Window_Dirty (Laser marker: the protective window has fumed up, marks come out faint) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Lens (Window lamp: tells the operator to clean the laser window) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Window_Dirty) Examine If Closed asks: true when Window_Dirty is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Lens) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Lens on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 28
rungs.comment: FAULT LAMP: a lost result, a missed trigger, the camera off line, or three mismatches in a row

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is off, Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on, Cam1:I.Online is on and Code_Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Fault is on.

rungs.words: When either (Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on), (Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on), (Cam1:I.Online is off) or (Code_Fault (Three mismatches in a row: the line stops until START) is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Missed_Acq) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Cam1:I.Online) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Online is off.
    Path 4
    1. XIC(Code_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Code_Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Code_Fault.desc: Three mismatches in a row: the line stops until START

Laser_On.desc: Laser marker: arm the laser (its interlock); no mark while 0

Coder_Lot.desc: Laser marker: the lot number for the message

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

Rel_T.desc: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

Next_Ser.desc: The serial of the last bottle released

Ser_Q.desc: The serials of the bottles between the hopper and the marker, oldest first

PE_Coder.desc: The marker head's eye: a bottle is under the head

Coder_Serial.desc: Laser marker: the serial for the message (loaded with Load_Msg)

Coder_Msg_Ready.desc: Laser marker: the message carries Lot_No

Coder_Ready.desc: Laser marker ready: armed and not loading

Coder_Load.desc: Laser marker: load Lot_No into the message (rising edge, 0.5 s)

Mark_Ser.desc: The serial of the bottle at the marker

Cam_Q.desc: The serials marked, between the marker and the camera, oldest first

Coder_Mark.desc: Laser marker: mark the message on the bottle under the head (rising edge)

PE_Trigger.desc: Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view

Trig_Req.desc: A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection

Cam_Ser.desc: The serial the camera should read on the bottle it is inspecting

Read_Ser.desc: The serial read back: characters 7-9 of the string in Inspection_Results bytes 12-27

Res_Code.desc: The result of the bottle just inspected: the camera's bits, plus 128 for a mismatch

Mismatch.desc: The read-back is not what was sent

Mismatch_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar and the console: marks that did not read back as sent

Res_Q.desc: The result codes between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first

PE_Reject.desc: Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher

Cur.desc: The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher

Fire.desc: Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected

Reject_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected

Pass_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through

Window_Dirty.desc: Laser marker: the protective window has fumed up, marks come out faint

Lamp_Lens.desc: Window lamp: tells the operator to clean the laser window
